The Company develops, finances, constructs, owns, and operates utility-scale renewable energy projects across solar, wind, and energy storage. Enlight operates in the United States, Israel, and Europe. Enlight has been traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE: ENLT) since 2010 and has been listed on Nasdaq following its U.S. IPO in 2023 (Nasdaq: ENLT).

analysis_md:
# ENLT — Enlight Renewable Energy Ltd.
Engine 5.5.0 run, 2026-10-20. Price $69.17 (nasdaq_quote_api); market cap $9.173B (key_numbers.md, basis: diluted_latest; price × shares ÷ ads_ratio) — in scope under $40B. Israeli foreign private issuer, 20-F filer reporting under IFRS in USD (SIC 4911, Electric Services); the Nasdaq-traded security is the ordinary share itself (see ADS_RATIO_APPLIED).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json or statements.json — none are recomputed. Guidance and quarter figures are from the company's Q2 2026 release via search results, as noted.

## What it is
Utility-scale renewable independent power producer headquartered in Rosh Ha'ayin, Israel: develops, finances, constructs, owns and operates solar PV, wind and energy-storage projects across the US, Europe and MENA. Revenue is mostly contracted power sales under long-term PPAs plus, in recent years, US tax benefits and gains on partial sell-downs of project clusters (the Sunlight cluster) booked inside "revenues and income". Q2 2026 release: total portfolio 21.8 GW of generation and 74.6 GWh of storage; mature portfolio ~53% US, 32% Europe, 15% MENA; ~90% of operating capacity contracted under PPAs, a meaningful share inflation-indexed.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (20-F via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** revenue $488,596,000; net income (ProfitLoss) $160,702,000; operating cash flow $282,648,000; capex $1,812,570,000 (tag: PurchaseOfPropertyPlantAndEquipmentClassifiedAsInvestingActivities, rollup — key_numbers.md capex basis FY2025: $1.813B); SBC $10,470,000 (tag: AdjustmentsForSharebasedPayments — always a real cost); D&A $149,922,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $-1,540,392,000 = $-11.62/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $-11.62, latest FY OE total $-1.540B).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC) prints $951,033,000 (financials_history.csv) — not usable here: it caps capex at D&A of $149,922,000 while PP&E net actually rose from $3,699,192,000 (FY2024) to $6,281,418,000 (FY2025). The construction spend is real cash out the door; the conservative definition is the honest one for this screen.
- OE/share by year (financials_history.csv): FY2021 $-4.53, FY2022 $-5.75, FY2023 $-4.39, FY2024 $-5.29, FY2025 $-11.62. **OE-positive years (last 5): 0/5** (key_numbers.md).
- **Base used = normalized (3-yr median) OE/share $-5.29** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). No TTM base: ttm.py exits 3 for this filer (IFRS 20-F, no 10-Q XBRL facts — it refuses rather than zero-filling), so the median base stands per the worker spec for IFRS filers. The latest FY ($-11.62) is worse than the median, so the median is the generous choice and the verdict does not rest on it.
- Balance sheet (FY2025, financials_history.csv / statements.json): cash $528,497,000; engine net debt $1.240B on a CURRENT_ONLY basis (see data note below); total liabilities $6,634,964,000 against total equity $1,994,938,000; lease liabilities $243,531,000; total assets $8,629,902,000. Consolidated figures include non-controlling interests (minority interest $306,797,000 in statements.json — project-level partners created by the sell-down model): a method limit of the screen, noted here; it does not change an F verdict on a $-1.540B OE total.
- Post-FY2025 prints (Q2 2026 release, search results): Q2 revenues and income $210M (+55% YoY), adjusted EBITDA $160M (+67%), net income $31M, operating cash flow $84M (+37%); H1 2026 revenues and income $409M (+55%), operating cash flow $185M (+48%); full-year 2026 guidance raised to $790–820M revenue and $565–585M adjusted EBITDA. Growth is real — and the company remains in a heavy construction phase (4.5 FGW under construction at the release date), so there is no evidence TTM owner's earnings have turned positive.

## Moat: 4/10 — weak-moderate, contracted but not yet earning its cost of capital
Justification: long-term PPAs (15–25 years, ~90% of operating capacity contracted, partly inflation-indexed) and a diversified US/Europe/MENA pipeline give real revenue visibility, and execution is proven ($2.6B CO Bar financing closed Q2 2026; 5th-largest US utility-scale solar-plus-storage developer by pipeline, S&P Global Commodity Insights). Capped at 4 on the ROIC evidence: fundamentals.json roic_proxy ran 5.43% (FY2020), 4.43% (FY2021), 5.70% (FY2022), 7.29% (FY2023), 9.32% (FY2024), 8.07% (FY2025) — at or below the cost of capital through the whole window — and gross margin on the clean pre-sell-down years was 54–60% (FY2020 57.4%, FY2021 59.8%, FY2022 57.8%, FY2023 54.4% in fundamentals.json; FY2024–25's 78.6%/72.5% are inflated by tax benefits and Sunlight sell-down gains inside "revenues and income", not by power-sale pricing power).
- FOR: Long-term contracted cash flows: ~90% of operating capacity under PPAs of 15–25 years, a meaningful share inflation-indexed (Q2 2026 release); Diversified platform: mature portfolio ~53% US, 32% Europe, 15% MENA; total portfolio 21.8 GW generation plus 74.6 GWh storage (Q2 2026 release); Development and financing execution at scale: $2.6B CO Bar complex financing closed in Q2 2026; ranked 5th-largest US utility-scale solar-plus-storage developer by pipeline (S&P Global Commodity Insights); Storage position: early mover in grid-scale storage, including wins in Israel's first high-voltage storage availability tender (300 MW AC).
- AGAINST: ROIC proxy only 4.4%–9.3% across FY2020–FY2025 (fundamentals.json) — at or below the cost of capital through the cycle so far; no pricing power beyond contracted PPA prices; Development inputs are contestable — land, interconnection, panels, turbines and storage are bought in competitive markets against NextEra, Brookfield and other scaled platforms; Returns hinge on tax credits, regulated tenders and financing costs: finance costs rose to $164,730,000 in FY2025 (+52.7% YoY, statements.json); Capital hunger dilutes: capex $1,812,570,000 in FY2025 vs operating cash flow $282,648,000, funded by project debt plus repeated equity placements (share count +9.9%/yr).
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years (key_numbers.md): growth would hold 2 years, then converge linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years — moot on a negative base, recorded for the file.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-20)
No scenario table exists: with a negative normalized base the engine produces no scenarios, no IV and no IRR (score.json: scenarios {}, iv_at_15 null, implied_irr null). Tier by numbers: **F**, sub-type **no_cash_generation** — "sum of the last 3 fiscal years (the median window)" of OCF − capex is not positive (dcf_numbers.json).
- Probabilities 10/25/30/25/10 and the default offsets/multipliers are recorded in judgment.json for form only; they price nothing on a negative base.
- Growth sanity check (required even here): the engine's growth blend is 31.48% (rev CAGR 5y 47.36%, rev CAGR 3y 36.48%, latest rev YoY 29.28% — key_numbers.md) and current prints are hotter (Q2 2026 revenues and income +55% YoY; 2026 revenue guided to $790–820M vs $488,596,000 in FY2025). No scenario start was set below a recent print — but growth is not the binding variable: FY2025 capex was $1,812,570,000 against operating cash flow of $282,648,000, so owner's earnings stay negative at any of these growth rates until the build pace normalizes. A start below the latest print would need a written reason in a scored run; here there is nothing to score.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): resolved by evidence, not by a TTM pin. ttm.py was run and exits 3 for this IFRS 20-F filer (no 10-Q XBRL facts; it refuses to zero-fill), so the median base is used and stated as such, per the spec for IFRS filers. The interim evidence is the Q2 2026 release (6-K): H1 2026 revenues and income $409M (+55%) and operating cash flow $185M (+48%) with 4.5 FGW still under construction — the build phase, and therefore the capex drag, continues; nothing in the interim prints suggests a positive TTM OE the FY2025 base is missing.
- **DILUTION** (share count growing 9.9%/yr; share count CAGR 9.87%, growth adj -5.00% in key_numbers.md): the dilution is paid-in growth equity, not SBC — SBC was only $10,470,000 in FY2025 ($8,360,000 FY2024, $4,970,000 FY2023, financials_history.csv). Shares diluted rose from 98,108,669 (FY2021) to 132,619,069 (FY2025) through placements (an ~NIS 1B private placement in August 2025; a further 6,002,416 ordinary shares at NIS 220 in February 2026 per the company's 6-K, search results) that fund the project build. The -5% growth adjustment is already in the blend; the real cost is that per-share OE gets worse even as total revenue compounds.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump in the last 5 yrs): the jump is FY2022 revenue +87.56% (statements.json revenue growth), off a small base ($102,461,000 in FY2021) as newly built projects commissioned and the US developer Clēnera (acquired 2021; acquisitions were $156,496,000 of FY2021 investing outflow in statements.json) consolidated. No divestiture or restatement drives it, and it cannot distort the verdict: OE/share is negative in every year on every basis, before and after the jump. The one real basis caveat is composition, not scale: FY2024–25 "revenues and income" include Sunlight sell-down gains and US tax benefits, which flatter revenue growth and gross margin — noted under Moat; the OCF-based OE series is unaffected in sign.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income vs operating cash flow >40% apart in 2023, 2024): structural, not a one-off. FY2023: net income $98,041,000 vs operating cash flow $191,599,000; FY2024: $66,505,000 vs $255,279,000 (financials_history.csv). The gap is mainly the non-cash D&A add-back as the fleet depreciates — D&A $65,796,000 in FY2023 and $108,889,000 in FY2024 — plus IFRS finance-cost and working-capital presentation (ΔNWC -$166,938,000 in FY2023, +$50,930,000 in FY2024). No tax deposit or impairment one-off was found. Resolution: the conservative OE base is built on OCF directly, and OCF running *above* net income flatters the base — the base is still $-5.29/share, so the divergence does not manufacture the F.
- **ADS_RATIO_APPLIED** (x1.0): the FY2025 20-F cover registers "Ordinary shares, NIS 0.1 par value" under ENLT on Nasdaq, with 132,133,899 ordinary shares outstanding at December 31, 2025 — there is no ADS program; the traded security is the ordinary share itself (dual-listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange), so per-share figures and the $69.17 price are on the same basis with no scaling. Recorded as the ads_ratio field in judgment.json (filing statement in the filer's own 20-F), per the bounded authority in step 8 (d).
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly): accepted, confidence low, model_fit "misfit" in score.json. The misfit is real and named: nearly all of the $1,812,570,000 FY2025 capex is growth capex for plants not yet generating, so OCF − total capex punishes a developer mid-build. Sized to the conservative end anyway: even on the operating business alone, FY2025 operating cash flow of $282,648,000 is a thin cash return on a $6,281,418,000 net PP&E base, ROIC proxy is 8.07%, and the equity is priced at $69.17 for a growth story (2026–28 commissioning, storage scale-up, eventual capex normalization), not for current owner's earnings. The F is this screen's answer, not a claim the projects are worthless.

## Data note — debt tags
The engine's net debt ($1.240B, key_numbers.md) carries basis CURRENT_ONLY (CurrentPortionOfLongtermBorrowings + ShorttermBorrowings): no long-term debt tag was read (debt_lt blank in financials_history.csv), so that figure understates borrowings. Stated from the filing instead (statements.json / financials_history.csv): total liabilities were $6,634,964,000 at FY2025 (current liabilities $1,629,205,000), total equity $1,994,938,000, cash $528,497,000, lease liabilities $243,531,000. The bulk of the non-current liabilities is long-term project financing the engine's tag list does not capture. Leverage is therefore materially higher than the engine's net-debt line suggests — one more reason the verdict is sized conservatively; it cannot rescue a negative OE base in any case.

## My thoughts / overlay
- This is the classic IPP build-phase F: revenue compounding at 29–55%, adjusted EBITDA margins the market loves, and owner's earnings deeply negative because every dollar of OCF — and several dollars of new debt and equity besides — goes straight into new plants. The screen cannot credit 2028's commissioned fleet; it can only note that the equity story requires capex to normalize toward D&A while the commissioned base keeps its contracted cash flows.
- The refresh trigger is concrete: a fiscal year in which capex falls toward the $149,922,000 D&A line while OCF follows the guided revenue path ($790–820M for 2026) would flip OE positive. Until a filed year prints that, there is no hurdle-clearing price to quote — on a negative base, IV@15% is not computed at any price.
- Dilution is the quiet tax on the story: share count +9.87%/yr means total OE must not merely turn positive, it must outrun a count that has grown from 98,108,669 to 132,619,069 in four years, plus the February 2026 placement on top.
